title: Compute In-Memory System Engineer Intern
description: Change the world. Love your job. At TI, Systems engineers focus deeply on understanding the technical needs, and future trends of an industry or end equipment, then create new products and innovative forward-looking product roadmaps to solve them. Systems Engineers are an integral part each phase of new product development at TI. In the early stages of product development, systems engineers interface with key stakeholders (customer decision-makers, application engineers, marketing, management, sales, IC design engineers, technology development) to negotiate specifications, perform trade-offs, understand the competitive landscape, and ultimately develop detailed technical definitions for new products. They then collaborate with the full IC development team (design, applications, test, product engineers) to deliver products to the market which are compelling, competitive, cost-conscious, manufacturable, and importantly, successful in growing TI’s business. We are seeking a highly motivated PhD student to join our Embedded AI team in Kilby Labs this summer to work on cutting-edge digital compute in-memory (CIM) research and development for resource-constrained microcontroller applications. As a key member of our team, you will focus on advancing energy-efficient computing architectures that enable intelligent edge processing on cost and power-constrained platforms, including architectures that tile and scale digital CIM to deliver much higher compute throughput. Your work will involve exploring innovative approaches to co-optimize algorithms, architectures, and hardware implementations for CIM systems. In this systems engineering intern role, you’ll have the chance to: Research and develop novel digital compute in-memory (CIM) architectures optimized for edge AI workloads on resource-constrained microcontrollers Explore tiling of digital CIM macros, ganging multiple CIM tiles together to scale compute throughput well beyond a single macro while staying within strict area, power and cost budgets Study inter-tile architecture trade-offs: dataflow, workload partitioning and mapping across tiles, tile-to-tile communication, scheduling, and utilization Quantify throughput, energy efficiency (TOPS/W) and area scaling of tiled CIM versus conventional NPU/MAC-array approaches, including the impact of mixed-precision and sub-8-bit quantization Explore algorithm-hardware co-design techniques to maximize energy efficiency and computational throughput Collaborate with internal technology and design teams to simulate and validate CIM-based solutions Develop and optimize machine learning models and inference flows tailored for in-memory computing paradigms Participate in the design and implementation of software toolchains and simulation frameworks for CIM and tiled-CIM evaluation Investigate memory hierarchy optimizations and data movement reduction strategies for edge processing Document findings and present trade-offs and recommendations to architecture, design and business stakeholders Minimum Requirements: Currently pursuing a PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electrical and Computer Engineering or related field Cumulative 3.0/4.0 GPA or higher Preferred Qualifications: Solid background in computer architecture, digital design, memory systems, and/or embedded systems Research experience in compute in-memory (CIM), processing-in-memory (PIM) or near-memory computing, ideally demonstrated by publications at leading architecture/circuits/systems venues (e.g., ISCA, MICRO, HPCA, DAC, ISSCC) Familiarity with scalable / multi-tile accelerator architectures, including dataflow, mapping and scheduling of neural networks across multiple compute tiles Proficiency in hardware description languages (Verilog/VHDL) and/or architectural simulation tools Strong programming skills in Python and C/C++, including performance analysis and optimization Experience with machine learning model optimization, quantization (including sub-8-bit), and deployment on resource-constrained devices Knowledge of SRAM/DRAM circuit design and memory architecture principles Familiarity with deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) and embedded ML libraries (e.g., TensorFlow Lite, CMSIS-NN) Understanding of energy-efficient computing techniques and power/area modeling Experience with algorithm-hardware co-design methodologies Ability to establish strong relationships with key stakeholders critical to success, both internally and externally Strong verbal and written communication skills to audiences of varied background Ability to simplify complex problems and navigate uncertainty Ability to quickly ramp on new systems and processes Demonstrated strong interpersonal, analytical and problem-solving skills Ability to work in teams and collaborate effectively with people in different functions Ability to take the initiative and drive for results Strong time management skills that enable on-time project delivery Why TI? The future starts here. As a TIer, you'll play a critical role in defining the next era of semiconductor technology and help create the innovations that shape the world around us. Surround yourself with a team of innovators who value your unique perspective and will challenge you to bring your best self to work every day. We believe that fostering a culture of collaboration fuels both personal growth and technological breakthroughs. Explore our company culture . At TI, your success goes beyond your work. Take advantage of comprehensive benefits designed to support your total well-being at work and in life, from competitive compensation to extensive health coverage and wellness programs. Learn more about our benefits offerings . About Texas Instruments Texas Instruments Incorporated (Nasdaq: TXN) is a global semiconductor company that designs, manufactures and sells analog and embedded processing chips for markets such as industrial, automotive, data center, personal electronics and communications equipment. At our core, we have a passion to create a better world by making electronics more affordable through semiconductors. This passion is alive today as each generation of innovation builds upon the last to make our technology more reliable, more affordable and lower power, making it possible for semiconductors to go into electronics everywhere.
